claims.claim: Vancouver recorded 6,008 net new homes between October 1, 2025 and September 30, 2026, nearly six percent above a target of 5,684.
claims.episode_span: Vancouver recorded 6,008 net new homes between October 1, 2025 and September 30, 2026
claims.source_title: City of Vancouver beats annual housing completion target, as new Conservative provincial government prepares to scrap BC NDP rules
claims.supporting_quote: A new City staff report notes that 6,008 net new homes reached completion over the legislated year-long reporting period between Oct. 1, 2025 and Sept. 30, 2026.

claims.claim: The city counted 6,809 completed units and subtracted 801 demolitions.
claims.episode_span: The city counted 6,809 completed units and subtracted 801 demolitions.
claims.source_title: City of Vancouver beats annual housing completion target
claims.supporting_quote: The City recorded 6,809 completed units and subtracted 801 demolished units to arrive at the net gain.

claims.claim: Vancouver has recorded 14,989 net new homes since October 2023, about 92 percent of a three-year target of 16,281.
claims.episode_span: Since October 2023 it has recorded 14,989 net new homes, about 92 percent of the three-year target of 16,281
claims.source_title: City of Vancouver beats annual housing completion target
claims.supporting_quote: Vancouver has recorded 14,989 net new homes since October 2023, reaching about 92 per cent of the cumulative three-year legislated target of 16,281.

claims.claim: Premier Lorne Doerkson directed a one-in, two-out regulatory rule and a return of requirements to 2017 levels in a November 24, 2026 mandate letter to Carson Binda.
claims.episode_span: In a November 24, 2026 mandate letter, Doerkson directs Binda to work with other ministers to bring provincial regulatory requirements back to 2017 levels
claims.source_title: B.C. premier seeks red tape rollback to 2017 levels, before NDP took power
claims.supporting_quote: In his Nov. 24, 2026 mandate letter, Doerkson directs Binda to work with other ministers to bring the provincial government’s regulatory requirements back to 2017 levels by the end of the administration’s current term.

claims.claim: Doug McCallum is running for Metro Vancouver chair and says he would work so local governments have no direct say over utilities.
claims.episode_span: McCallum says that if elected he would work with the B.C. Conservatives to turn Metro Vancouver into something unlike any other regional government
claims.source_title: Doug McCallum runs for Metro Vancouver chair — with the goal of eliminating his position
claims.supporting_quote: Doug McCallum promises that, if elected, he would work with the B.C. Conservatives to transition Metro Vancouver into something different than any other regional government in the province — one where local governments have no direct say over utilities.

claims.claim: The B.C. Court of Appeal ordered Stephen Brown to pay Rakesh Dhunna $4,262,369.40 after an uncompleted $18 million West Vancouver purchase.
claims.episode_span: The B.C. Court of Appeal has ordered Stephen Brown to pay Rakesh Dhunna $4,262,369.40
claims.source_title: Buyer fails to close on $18 million West Vancouver mansion, owes seller millions: B.C. Court of Appeal
claims.supporting_quote: Five years later, after a lengthy and convoluted court case, the B.C. Court of Appeal has ordered Brown to pay Dhunna the difference between the two sales prices, of $4,262,369.40.

claims.claim: A Greater Victoria B.C. Transit strike planned for Friday was averted by a Thursday agreement after job action since August.
claims.episode_span: A one-day B.C. Transit strike set for Friday in Greater Victoria will not go ahead.
claims.source_title: Strike averted: B.C. Transit and union come to agreement in Victoria
claims.supporting_quote: Workers had begun a series of job actions since August, with a one-day strike planned for Friday, before the two sides struck an agreement Thursday

claims.claim: Squamish is asking residents to limit indoor water use until further notice to manage sewer flows after a local state of emergency.
claims.episode_span: the District of Squamish is still asking residents to limit indoor water use until further notice
claims.source_title: District of Squamish asks residents to limit indoor water use after wet B.C. weather
claims.supporting_quote: The District of Squamish, which declared a state of local emergency over high tides and flood risk earlier this week, asks residents to limit indoor water use until further notice to help manage sewer flows.

claims.claim: Twelve First Nations are buying an indirect stake in Coastal GasLink backed by a $168-million federal loan guarantee.
claims.episode_span: Twelve First Nations in British Columbia are buying an indirect ownership stake in the Coastal GasLink pipeline
claims.source_title: 12 First Nations in B.C. buy stake in Coastal GasLink pipeline
claims.supporting_quote: A group of 12 First Nations in British Columbia are buying an indirect ownership stake in the Coastal GasLink Pipeline, backed by a $168-million loan guarantee from the federal Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program.

claims.claim: A November 25 civil lawsuit alleges Iain Hunt killed Trina Hunt near Port Moody in January 2021; he is charged with indignity to human remains, not murder, and the criminal trial is set for October 2027.
claims.episode_span: A lawsuit filed November 25 in B.C. Supreme Court in New Westminster alleges that Iain Hunt killed his wife, Trina Hunt
claims.source_title: Trina Hunt’s family alleges husband killed her, seeks return of assets in B.C. lawsuit
claims.supporting_quote: A new lawsuit filed in B.C.’s Supreme Court in New Westminster alleges that Iain Hunt killed his wife, Trina Hunt and should not be able to profit financially from her death.

claims.claim: Justin Littlewolfe was sentenced to seven years for shooting a B.C. doctor in the face and has just over three years left after credit.
claims.episode_span: Justin Littlewolfe was sentenced to seven years for shooting a B.C. doctor in the face
claims.source_title: Man who shot B.C. doctor in the face sentenced to seven years in prison
claims.supporting_quote: Justin Littlewolfe was sentenced to seven years in prison and with enhanced credit for time spent in custody since his arrest, he has just over three years left to serve.

claims.claim: Highway 1 from 256th Street in Langley to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford is closed until December 31, 2026, with a detour.
claims.episode_span: On Highway 1, the stretch from 256th Street in Langley to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford is closed around the clock until December 31, 2026
claims.source_title: DriveBC: 4 major road events in Metro Vancouver
claims.supporting_quote: Road construction from Highway 1, In Langley - District and 256th Street to In Abbotsford and Lefeuvre Road. Starting 12:00 AM PDT on Friday October 30, 2026 until 12:00 AM PCT on Thursday December 31, 2026. All day, every day. Closed. Detour in effect.

claims.claim: Vancouver's Friday forecast is cloudy, a 60 percent chance of morning showers, southeast wind 30 km/h becoming light, and a high of 10, with no watches or warnings.
claims.episode_span: Friday is cloudy with a 60 percent chance of showers this morning
claims.supporting_quote: Friday: Cloudy. 60 percent chance of showers this morning. Wind southeast 30 km/h becoming light this afternoon. High 10.

claims.claim: Amar Doman says the B.C. Lions are interested in owning or operating B.C. Place, which is owned by PavCo.
claims.episode_span: B.C. Lions owner Amar Doman says the club is interested in owning or operating B.C. Place
claims.source_title: B.C. Lions owner says team is interested in owning or operating Vancouver's B.C. Place
claims.supporting_quote: The stadium is owned by provincial Crown corporation PavCo, and its existence as a provincially-owned asset has rankled the stadium's other tenant, the Major League Soccer's Vancouver Whitecaps.
